the characterization of the effects of D-glucose upon the subsequent stimulation by nonnutrient secretagogs of Ca2+ outflow in pancreatic islets.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
glucose, in the presence of a nonnutrient secretagoge, enhances the sequestration and the release of Ca2+ into the cytosol of pancreatic beta cells.
D-glucose, in addition to its known effect upon insulin secretion, enhances the subsequent stimulation of Ca2+ efflux from pancreatic islets evoked by nonnutrient secretagoues.

glucose enhances the ability of the islet cells to respond to nonnutrient secretogogues.
glucose, in a concentration-dependent manner, enhances the ability of nonnutrient secretagoues to stimulate 45 Ca outflow from pancreatic islets.

glucose, in prelabelled islet cells, increases the magnitude of the increment in Ca2+ efflux evoked in response to nonnutrient secretagoues, such as sulfonylurea or a high concentration of K+.
